input: nums is a nonempty dense Array of finite integer Number values in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], with length <= 4294967294 so that length + 1 is a valid Array length. k is a safe integer with 1 <= k <= the number of distinct values. Counts and indices stay exact within this domain. The integer domain does not distinguish -0 from 0; Map canonicalizes that key to 0. NaN, infinities, BigInt, sparse arrays and non-integers are outside the domain. Inputs are not validated.
return: Type: fresh Array of k distinct integer Number values. Every selected frequency is at least every unselected frequency; compare the selected values without requiring a particular output order. Descending frequency, with equal-frequency values ordered by first occurrence in nums. If a tie crosses k, the earliest first occurrences are selected. Exact sequence equality under integer-value comparison is expected between these two candidates on their shared domain, independently of order-insensitive problem acceptance.
mutation_aliasing: Input mutation: none. The returned Array is newly allocated and never aliases nums; every bucket is a separately allocated Array. No persistent Solution instance state.
numeric: Exact safe-integer Number counts and indices; no bitwise coercions. Values lie in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991] on the shared domain; n <= 4294967294. Signed-zero identity is not distinguished.
complexity: n = nums.length; u = number of distinct values O(n) expected under expected constant-time Map operations; ECMAScript itself does not promise this hash-table bound. No sorting is performed. O(n): n + 1 bucket Arrays, u Map entries, and exactly u stored bucket values in total. The output contains k values.
